title: Removing a pro-prime-to-ell factor from condensed derived invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $V$, put $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. For a topological group $J$, write $\mathcal A_F(J)$ for internal $C_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,J)$; invariants are the equalizer imposing that action to be trivial, and $R\Gamma_J$ is their ordinary total right derived functor in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $B,L$ be profinite groups, and suppose every finite continuous quotient of $B$ has order prime to $\ell$. Let $V$ have a continuous $E$-linear $B\times L$-action whose $B$-image $Q$ is finite of order prime to $\ell$. Give $V^B$ its subspace topology and its residual $L$-action. The canonical inflation morphism
$$a_F:R\Gamma_L((V^B)_F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F),$$
induced by $B\times L\to L$ and $(V^B)_F\hookrightarrow V_F$, is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. On degree-zero invariants it is the inclusion, hence the identity after identifying both invariant objects. It is natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $V$. For $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the square formed by $a_E$, $\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega$ and the canonical derived coefficient maps induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ commutes. Here and below the coefficient map to a restricted derived invariant object is obtained by deriving the natural equality of invariants with scalar restriction. If $B$ is trivial, $a_F$ is the identity under the evident identifications.

proof.text: Write $\rho:B\to\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ for the action. Its kernel $K$ is open and normal: the finite set $\rho(B)$ is discrete as a subspace of the Hausdorff finite-dimensional matrix space, and $\rho$ is continuous. Thus $B/K=Q$. Every finite continuous quotient $K/H$ has order prime to $\ell$: $H$ is open in $B$, and its core $H_0=\bigcap_{b\in B}bHb^{-1}$ is a finite intersection because $[B:H]<\infty$. Then $B/H_0$ is a finite continuous quotient of $B$, and $K/H$ is a quotient of its subgroup $K/H_0$. Choose an $E$-basis of $V$, of size $d$. The corresponding maps $F\otimes_E V\cong F^d$ and their inverses are continuous matrices, so $V_F\cong C_F^d$ as $K$-modules with trivial action. If $d=0$ these are zero objects.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-condensed-acyclicity] to $K$. It gives the canonical scalar augmentation $C_F[0]\to R\Gamma_K(C_F[0])$ as an isomorphism for both $F$. The same holds for $V_F$: take $d$ copies of a K-injective resolution of $C_F$; their finite direct sum is K-injective since a chain map from an acyclic complex to it is a tuple of $d$ null-homotopic maps, whose homotopies form a tuple. Termwise invariants preserve finite sums. Under the basis identification the augmentation is therefore the direct sum of $d$ scalar augmentations. This argument uses only finite sums, including the empty sum, and the resolution computation of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 2

proof.text: For $G=B$ use [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] with this $K$ and the given $L$, and write $T_F$ for its kernel invariants functor. Since $K$ acts trivially on $V_F$, $T_F(V_F)$ is $V_F$ with the residual $Q\times L$-action. The underlying map of $\eta_F:T_F(V_F)[0]\to RT_F(V_F[0])$ is exactly the augmentation in step 2, hence is an isomorphism. Use the generated Grothendieck action site of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] over the small coherent profinite site; its base has finite limits and its group and coefficient ring are sheaves. Forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels and detects zero by the final paragraph of that statement, so the cohomology of the cone vanishes before forgetting whenever it vanishes after forgetting. Consequently $\eta_F$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal A_{Q\times L}(C_F))$. The normalized equation $c_F\operatorname{inf}_F=R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(\eta_F)$ now proves that $\operatorname{inf}_F:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(V_F)\to R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 3

proof.text: Put $m=|Q|$. For any internal $C_F$-module $M$ with $Q\times L$-action, the finite sum $e_M=m^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q}q$ defines an internal $L$-equivariant idempotent. A continuous $Q$-valued section is locally constant on a finite clopen partition; on each piece multiplication permutes the finite sum. Hence $\operatorname{im}e_M=M^Q$ for the full condensed notion of fixed sections. The scalar $m^{-1}$ is a continuous constant section of $C_F$, so is available also for $F=\Omega$. Invariants are left exact by [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. They preserve epimorphisms as well: an invariant section of a target has a local lift through an epimorphism of module sheaves, and averaging that lift gives an invariant lift of the same section. Here [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] uses the generated Grothendieck action topology and identifies the underlying cokernel with the sheafification on the base profinite site of the sectionwise cokernel. Thus the lifts are local on the base site; no composition property of the unsaturated action precoverage is needed. Thus $\Gamma_Q^L:\mathcal A_{Q\times L}(C_F)\to\mathcal A_L(C_F)$ is exact. This finite sum uses no integration over an infinite group.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 4

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] with $G=K=Q$ and quotient $1$. Its comparison reads $R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(M)\cong R\Gamma_L(R\Gamma_Q^L(M))$. Exactness from step 4 and the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identify $R\Gamma_Q^L(M[0])$ with $M^Q[0]$, through the canonical map. The normalized inflation equation therefore makes $b_F:R\Gamma_L(V_F^Q)\to R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(V_F)$ an isomorphism. On $V$, the finite average $e=m^{-1}\sum_q\rho(q)$ has image $V^B$; both its inclusion and its projection are continuous linear maps. Tensoring this splitting with $F$ identifies $F\otimes_E V^B$ with $\operatorname{im}(1\otimes e)$, with the subspace topology (choose a basis of the image and kernel). Applying continuous maps on every profinite test set proves $(V^B)_F=V_F^Q$, including residual $L$-actions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 5

proof.text: The composite $\operatorname{inf}_F b_F$ has source $R\Gamma_L((V^B)_F)$ and target $R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F)$. The composition clause of [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] identifies it with the canonical inflation $a_F$ for $B\times L\to Q\times L\to L$ and the invariant inclusion. Thus $a_F$ is an isomorphism. Its degree-zero map is the original inclusion: the ordinary normalized transposes restrict codomain to invariants and their inverses compose with inclusion. Both source and target invariant submodules are the same $L$-fixed part of $V_F^B$, so this map is the identity after that identification.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 6

proof.text: All maps used are canonical resolution maps, normalized inflation maps, or invariant inclusions. For an equivariant continuous $E$-linear map $f:V\to W$, $f\rho_V(b)=\rho_W(b)f$ implies $f(V^B)\subseteq W^B$ and equality of the two composites with invariant inclusions. The naturality clause of [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison], applied directly to $a_F$ viewed as the single quotient $B\to1$, gives the requested naturality without choosing a common finite image or compatible bases. The coefficient clause of that node applied to $C_E\to C_\Omega$ and $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ gives $u_{B\times L}a_E=(\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega)u_L$. The invariant identifications of step 5 respect this map since $e_\Omega(1\otimes v)=1\otimes e_E(v)$, term by term in the same finite sum. Thus this is precisely the coefficient square in the statement, in ordinary condensed modules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 7

proof.text: If $B=1$, then $K=Q=1$, both kernel augmentations and the normalized comparisons in [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] are identities; invariant inclusion is also the identity. The composite in step 6 is therefore the identity. If $V=0$ the constructions are zero, and if $V^B=0$ step 5 gives zero derived invariants for $Q\times L$ and hence step 3 gives zero derived invariants for $B\times L$. No completeness assertion about $\Omega$ has been used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 8
